hero.headline: Oil Prices Climb as U.S. and Iran Exchange Strikes
hero.body:
Oil prices rose following a fresh round of military exchanges between the United States and Iran in the Persian Gulf region. Iranian drones struck Kuwait's main international airport, damaging civilian buildings and killing at least one person. The attack represents the latest escalation in a series of strikes that have strained a fragile ceasefire between the two countries.

The incident began when U.S. forces fired a Hellfire missile at a tanker attempting to breach the American blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. military officials then reported repelling Iranian retaliatory attacks in the region and striking sites on Iran's Qeshm Island. In response, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps claimed it attacked the U.S. Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain with missiles and drones, though U.S. Central Command denied the attack was successful.

Kuwait briefly closed its main airport following the drone strike. As a significant oil producer generating more than two million barrels per day, any disruption to Kuwaiti infrastructure carries immediate consequences for global energy supplies. The country also hosts American military personnel and serves as a key U.S. ally in regional security arrangements.

The exchange of strikes underscores the lack of political progress in resolving Middle East tensions, despite recent claims by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio that a ceasefire deal with Tehran was within reach. Rubio told the Senate Foreign Relations Committee that Iran had agreed to negotiate aspects of its nuclear program previously off the table.

However, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi rejected these characterizations of progress. He stated that any ceasefire must cover all fronts, including Lebanon, and that violations on any front constitute violations across all fronts. Araghchi held the United States and Israel responsible for consequences stemming from any breach of the agreement.

The strikes come at a particularly sensitive moment for global energy markets. The Persian Gulf region accounts for a substantial portion of worldwide oil production, and military conflict threatens major shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz as well as production facilities. Previous escalations between the U.S. and Iran have historically created significant volatility in energy markets.

Traders responded to the attacks by pushing oil prices higher as they assessed potential disruptions to Middle East energy supplies. The fragile state of the ceasefire and the series of tit-for-tat military strikes suggest energy markets may remain volatile in coming days as developments unfold in the region.

Both countries now face critical decisions about whether to continue military operations or pursue diplomatic de-escalation efforts.

cards.headline: Ukraine Strikes St. Petersburg as Putin Economic Forum Opens
cards.teaser: Ukrainian forces targeted a navy base and oil terminal in the region containing Russia's second-largest city on the opening day of an annual economic conference.
cards.body:
Ukraine struck St. Petersburg early Wednesday with long-range drones targeting oil storage facilities and military sites as Putin's annual economic forum opened. Several drones hit their targets after Russian air defenses attempted unsuccessfully to intercept them, causing explosions and sending black smoke across the city from burning oil terminals.

The timing of the attacks coincided with the arrival of international guests for the flagship economic event, where Putin is scheduled to speak on Friday. President Zelensky said Ukrainian forces had targeted a navy base and oil terminal in the region that includes Russia's second-largest city.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Announces Tariffs on 59 Countries Over Forced Labor
cards.teaser: The administration plans to impose levies of up to 12.5 percent on countries that have not taken action against goods made with forced labor.
cards.body:
Trump administration officials announced plans to impose tariffs of between 10 and 12.5 percent on 60 trading partners, including the UK, EU, Canada, Australia, and Taiwan. The administration cited failures to adequately address forced labor in manufacturing as the rationale for the levies.

The EU swiftly objected, stating that the tariffs violated a trade agreement reached in July and breached the spirit of that deal. The announcement represents Trump's latest effort to revive his signature trade policy following a February Supreme Court decision that struck down many of his previous tariffs.

cards.headline: White House moves to centralize control over billions in federal science grants
cards.teaser: The Office of Management and Budget is seeking authority over federal grant distribution in a move critics say threatens scientific independence.
cards.body:
The White House Office of Management and Budget has proposed new policies that would require political appointees to vet federal grants to universities and nongovernmental organizations. Under the plan, all grants approved by Trump appointees must "demonstrably advance the president's policy priorities" and meet standards for "American values" as defined by the president.

Scientists and experts have warned the proposal would undermine the integrity of American scientific research. The change shifts grant approval decisions from subject matter experts at scientific agencies to political appointees, raising concerns about how universities, research institutions, and independent scientists will receive federal support for their work.

cards.headline: Primary elections conclude in six states with key Democratic and Republican nominations decided
cards.teaser: Polls closed Tuesday in six states holding primary elections, with voters selecting nominees for Senate, gubernatorial, and congressional races ahead of the 202.
cards.body:
Polls closed Tuesday in six states holding primary elections to select nominees for Senate, gubernatorial, and congressional races ahead of the 2026 general election. In Iowa, Josh Turek secured the Democratic Senate nomination, defeating a rival who had criticized party leaders. Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor, positioning herself as the likely favorite in the general election.

In California, vote counting continued in major statewide races. Xavier Becerra and Steve Hilton led their respective Democratic and Republican primaries for governor, vying to replace term-limited Governor Gavin Newsom. Final results remained uncalled as of reporting time.

cards.headline: Macy's Reports Strongest Quarterly Growth in Four Years
cards.teaser: The retailer raised its annual guidance after posting its fourth consecutive quarter of sales gains.
cards.body:
Macy's reported its strongest first quarter growth in four years and raised its full-year outlook. The company has now posted sales gains for four straight quarters as its turnaround strategy continues to gain traction.

The results showed solid performance across all three of Macy's brands. The retailer lifted its annual guidance despite broader concerns about consumer spending, indicating confidence in its business momentum heading into the remainder of the year.

cards.headline: Blue Origin Faces Extended Launch Pad Repairs After Rocket Explosion
cards.teaser: SpaceX veterans weigh in on how long it will take to rebuild the facility as the company seeks to resume launches.
cards.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded on its launch pad at Cape Canaveral, Florida on Thursday night during a test. The explosion caused significant damage to the facility, requiring substantial rebuilding efforts.

Blue Origin has stated it aims to resume launches by year's end, though industry assessments suggest a longer timeline. Some space experts have indicated repairs could extend into 2028, given the extent of the damage to the launch pad infrastructure.

hero.headline: Ukraine Strikes St. Petersburg as Putin Economic Forum Opens
hero.teaser: Ukrainian forces targeted a navy base and oil terminal in the region containing Russia's second-largest city on the opening day of an annual economic conference.
hero.body:
Ukraine struck St. Petersburg early Wednesday with long-range drones targeting oil storage facilities and military sites as Putin's annual economic forum opened. Several drones hit their targets after Russian air defenses attempted unsuccessfully to intercept them, causing explosions and sending black smoke across the city from burning oil terminals.

The timing of the attacks coincided with the arrival of international guests for the flagship economic event, where Putin is scheduled to speak on Friday. President Zelensky said Ukrainian forces had targeted a navy base and oil terminal in the region that includes Russia's second-largest city.

cards.headline: Drone Strike on Bus Kills Seven in Russia-Controlled Ukraine
cards.teaser: A bus traveling between Moscow and Simferopol in occupied Crimea was hit by a drone attack, according to a Russian official.
cards.body:
A drone attack on a bus traveling between Moscow and Simferopol killed seven people, according to Russian officials. The bus was in a Russia-controlled area of Ukraine when it was struck.

The incident occurred on a route connecting Moscow to the capital of Russian-occupied Crimea. The attack targeted civilian transportation moving through territory Russia has held since its 2014 annexation of Crimea and subsequent military operations in Ukraine.

cards.headline: Violent Protests Erupt in UK Over Henry Nowak Murder Case
cards.teaser: Eleven police officers were injured as demonstrations turned violent in Britain, prompting calls for calm from political leaders.
cards.body:
Demonstrations erupted across the United Kingdom following the death of Henry Nowak, who was stabbed by Vickrum Digwa. The protests turned violent in locations including Southampton, with demonstrators throwing rocks and garbage cans at police officers. Eleven officers and a police dog were injured during the unrest.

British officials condemned the violence. A cabinet minister called the scenes "unacceptable," while the interior minister criticized the violent reaction to the student's death. Prime Minister Keir Starmer and other leaders urged calm as tensions continued to escalate.

cards.headline: Fire at New Delhi Hotel Kills at Least 21
cards.teaser: A blaze in a residential area of the Indian capital injured dozens more, with foreign nationals among the dead.
cards.body:
At least 21 people were killed in a fire at a hotel in New Delhi's residential area. Dozens more were injured in the blaze, according to authorities.

Many of the victims were South Asians who had traveled to India for medical treatment or to accompany relatives seeking healthcare services.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Proposes Tariffs on 59 Countries
cards.teaser: The United States announced plans for new tariffs of 10 percent or more on most trading partners following a forced labor investigation.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is proposing tariffs between 10% and 12.5% on approximately 60 trading partners, citing forced labor concerns. The targeted countries and regions include Canada, Mexico, the European Union, the United Kingdom, Australia, and Taiwan.

The EU has already responded, stating it expects the US to honor the tariff agreement reached in July and arguing that these new levies undermine that deal's spirit. Brazil faces even steeper tariffs at 25%, which the administration claims are justified by unreasonable trade practices that restrict US commerce.

cards.headline: Ukraine Strikes St. Petersburg as Putin Economic Forum Opens
cards.teaser: Ukrainian forces targeted a navy base and oil terminal in the region containing Russia's second-largest city on the opening day of an annual economic conference.
cards.body:
Ukrainian drones struck oil storage facilities and military sites in St. Petersburg early Wednesday as international guests arrived for Putin's annual economic forum. Multiple long-range drones targeted the city despite Russian air defense efforts to intercept them. Explosions lit up the sky and black smoke billowed from the burning oil terminal.

The timing of the attack coincided with the opening of Russia's flagship economic event, where Putin is scheduled to speak Friday. President Zelensky said Ukrainian forces had targeted a navy base and oil terminal in the region containing Russia's second-largest city.

hero.headline: Trump administration drops plan for $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund
hero.body:
The Trump administration will not move forward with a proposed $1.8 billion fund intended to compensate individuals who claimed they were targeted by federal investigations, according to acting Attorney General Todd Blanche. The decision comes after sustained pressure from Republican lawmakers who questioned the fund's legality and implementation.

The fund was part of a larger agreement involving IRS operations and had become increasingly controversial on Capitol Hill. Republican members of Congress expressed concerns about the compensation mechanism, arguing it lacked clear guidelines for determining who would qualify for payments and how claims would be evaluated. Lawmakers worried the fund could potentially be misused or exploited to reward political allies without adequate oversight.

The proposed fund faced scrutiny from both the House and Senate, with critics arguing it set a troubling precedent that future administrations could follow. The White House Office of Management and Budget had participated in negotiations over the fund as part of broader budget discussions with Congress.

Despite abandoning the compensation fund, the Trump administration preserved other elements of its IRS agreement. The White House secured a ban on tax investigations into certain matters, suggesting it achieved at least some of its key priorities in the final deal, even as it retreated from the more contentious compensation mechanism.

The decision represents a notable instance of the Trump administration yielding to pressure from members of its own party. Republican lawmakers maintained that the original proposal went too far and lacked sufficient safeguards. The lack of detailed criteria for distributing funds emerged as a central point of disagreement throughout congressional negotiations.

The administration has not yet indicated whether it plans to pursue alternative approaches to address what it views as concerns about federal investigations being weaponized for political purposes. The retreat on the compensation fund suggests the White House prioritized retaining the tax investigation restrictions over maintaining its compensation proposal.

The reversal highlights tensions within the Republican Party over how aggressively the administration should pursue its stated goals. While some party members shared the White House's concerns about federal investigations, they drew the line at creating a compensation fund they felt lacked adequate protections against misuse.

The IRS agreement remains significant for the Trump administration's broader agenda, particularly the provision limiting tax investigations into unspecified matters. This element of the deal apparently proved more defensible to Republican critics than the compensation fund, which generated unified opposition across the party.

The decision to drop the fund reflects the administration's willingness to compromise on controversial proposals when facing sustained congressional resistance, particularly from within its own party.

cards.headline: US and Iran exchange strikes as Kuwait reports casualty from Iranian drone attack
cards.teaser: Kuwait says one person died after drones struck civilian buildings including its international airport.
cards.body:
Iranian drones struck civilian buildings in Kuwait, including its international airport, killing one person. The attack forced Kuwait to briefly shut down its main airport due to heavy damage.

The strikes are part of ongoing military exchanges between the United States and Iran that have tested a fragile ceasefire in the Persian Gulf region. The attack on Kuwaiti civilian infrastructure represents an expansion of the conflict beyond direct US-Iran confrontation.

cards.headline: White House moves to centralize control over billions in federal science grants
cards.teaser: The Office of Management and Budget is seeking authority over federal grant distribution in a move critics say threatens scientific independence.
cards.body:
The White House Office of Management and Budget has proposed new policies that would require political appointees to vet federal grants to universities and nongovernmental organizations. Under the plan, all grants approved by Trump appointees must "demonstrably advance the president's policy priorities" and meet standards for "American values" as defined by the president.

Scientists and experts have warned the proposal would undermine the integrity of American scientific research. The change shifts grant approval decisions from subject matter experts at scientific agencies to political appointees, raising concerns about how universities, research institutions, and independent scientists will receive federal support for their work.

cards.headline: California governor's race remains too close to call after primary
cards.teaser: Hilton and Becerra appear positioned to advance to the general election, but final results have not been determined.
cards.body:
California's gubernatorial primary remained undecided as ballots continued to be counted. Three candidates emerged at the top of the crowded field: Republican Steve Hilton and Democrats Xavier Becerra and Tom Steyer.

The state's top-two primary system allows the leading vote-getters regardless of party affiliation to advance to the general election. Two Democratic candidates—San Jose Mayor Matt Mahan and former Los Angeles Mayor Antonio Villaraigosa—conceded shortly after polls closed.

cards.headline: Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass advances to runoff election
cards.teaser: Bass will face a challenger in a runoff after primary results showed no candidate secured a majority.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass won the primary election but failed to secure the majority needed to avoid a runoff. She will face either Spencer Pratt, a former reality TV star, or city council member Nithya Raman in November's general election. As of Tuesday evening, the second-place finisher between Pratt and Raman had not been determined.

The Los Angeles mayoral race was part of a broader primary election night across California and other states. In California's gubernatorial contest, results remained too close to call, with Republican Steve Hilton and Democrats Xavier Becerra and Tom Steyer leading early returns. Two Democratic candidates, San Jose Mayor Matt Mahan and former Los Angeles Mayor Antonio Villaraigosa, conceded shortly after polls closed.

cards.headline: Ukrainian drones strike oil facilities in St. Petersburg ahead of Putin economic forum
cards.teaser: Long-range drones hit oil storage sites near the city days before Vladimir Putin is scheduled to address an economic gathering.
cards.body:
Ukrainian drones struck an oil terminal in St. Petersburg, setting it ablaze, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The attack occurred as the city hosted Putin's annual economic forum.

Several long-range drones targeted oil storage facilities near Russia's second-largest city. The strikes took place days before Putin was scheduled to address the flagship economic gathering.

cards.headline: Thousands of Lloyds Banking Group customers report online banking outage
cards.teaser: Users of Lloyds, Halifax, and Bank of Scotland apps experienced problems accessing accounts.
cards.body:
Thousands of Lloyds Banking Group customers experienced online banking problems on Wednesday morning. The outage affected users trying to access Lloyds, Halifax, and Bank of Scotland apps and websites.

The disruption prevented customers from logging into their accounts and completing transactions during business hours. Lloyds Banking Group operates several major retail banking platforms across the United Kingdom.

cards.headline: Macy's Reports Strongest Quarterly Growth in Four Years
cards.teaser: The retailer raised its annual guidance after posting its fourth consecutive quarter of sales gains.
cards.body:

The results showed solid performance across all three of Macy's brands. The retailer lifted its annual guidance despite broader concerns about consumer spending, indicating confidence in its business momentum heading into the remainder of the year.

cards.headline: S&P 500 Closes at Record High as Stock Futures Hold Steady
cards.teaser: The benchmark index extended its winning streak to nine days before stock futures showed little movement overnight.
cards.body:
Stock futures held steady following the S&P 500's close at another record high. The benchmark index has achieved nine consecutive days of gains, marking its longest winning streak in a year.

Artificial intelligence stocks have been the primary driver of the rally, propelling the broader market to new heights. However, escalating tensions with Iran pose potential pressure on the winning streak as oil prices rise following exchanges of strikes between the two countries.

cards.headline: Bill Pulte Takes on Intelligence Role, Raising Questions About Housing Agenda
cards.teaser: The Federal Housing Finance Agency head will now also serve as acting intelligence director.
cards.body:
Bill Pulte, head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, has been named acting Director of National Intelligence. He will retain his housing leadership role while taking on the intelligence position.

The dual appointments raise questions about Pulte's ability to focus on housing policy. He has already faced challenges advancing his housing market agenda at the FHFA, and the additional intelligence responsibilities may further stretch his attention during a period of continued pressure in the housing sector.

cards.headline: Lloyds Banking Group Apps Experience Widespread Outage
cards.teaser: Thousands of customers reported problems accessing online banking services across Lloyds, Halifax, and Bank of Scotland.
cards.body: Thousands of Lloyds Banking Group customers experienced disruptions to their mobile banking services on Wednesday morning. The outage affected users of Lloyds, Halifax, and Bank of Scotland apps, preventing access to online accounts across the three banking brands.

cards.headline: Blue Origin Faces Extended Launch Pad Repairs After Rocket Explosion
cards.teaser: SpaceX veterans weigh in on how long it will take to rebuild the facility as the company seeks to resume launches.
cards.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded on its launch pad at Cape Canaveral, Florida on Thursday night during a test. The explosion caused significant damage to the facility, requiring substantial rebuilding efforts.

Blue Origin has stated it aims to resume launches by year's end, though industry assessments suggest a longer timeline. Some space experts have indicated repairs could extend into 2028, given the extent of the damage to the launch pad infrastructure.

hero.headline: Nvidia and Microsoft launch RTX Spark laptops with new AI chips
hero.body:
Nvidia has unveiled the RTX Spark, a new superchip designed to bring artificial intelligence capabilities directly into laptops and desktop computers. The chip represents a significant expansion of Nvidia's reach beyond its dominant position in data center processors.

The RTX Spark combines a microprocessor and graphics chip, developed with assistance from Taiwan's MediaTek. Unlike current systems that rely on cloud computing for AI tasks, the new chip enables AI agents to run locally on personal computers. This allows these agents to navigate PCs autonomously, potentially replacing traditional mouse and keyboard interactions.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced the development at the Computex conference in Taiwan, describing it as reinventing the PC "for the first time in 40 years." The chip will launch this year and be integrated into devices from major computer manufacturers including Dell, Lenovo, Asus, and HP, running on Microsoft's Windows software. The collaboration between Nvidia and Microsoft has spanned three years.

Despite the chip's powerful capabilities, Nvidia states that computers using it will remain thin and lightweight. The company designed the RTX Spark to handle demanding AI processing while maintaining the portability users expect from modern laptops.

This move positions Nvidia in direct competition with established PC chip makers including Intel, Apple, Qualcomm, and AMD. Industry analysts have drawn comparisons between this moment and major technological shifts like the iPhone's launch and the emergence of ChatGPT.

Neil Shah, co-founder of Counterpoint Research, characterized the RTX Spark as potentially transformative. "The RTX Spark looks to transform the traditional app-centric PC to a real useful agentic AI personal computer which will eventually be in every home in coming years as private edge AI agents become pivotal," Shah said.

Nvidia is also developing the Vera CPU, another processor designed for AI agents. Early adopters of Vera include OpenAI, Anthropic, and SpaceX.

The expansion reflects Nvidia's broader strategy to extend its influence across multiple layers of the AI technology stack. While the company currently dominates the market for AI infrastructure and data center computing power, industry observers view the consumer PC market as a longer-term opportunity. Analyst Susannah Streeter noted that Nvidia's foray into personal computers "marks a bold attempt to extend its dominance beyond datacentres and into consumers' everyday lives," though investors likely see this as a growth opportunity rather than an immediate earnings driver.

Competing manufacturers are responding to Nvidia's push. Intel intends to ship an AI chip later this year that uses cheaper memory and cooling technology. The company announced a new graphics processing unit called Xe3P, codenamed Crescent Island, which is "purpose-built for this upcoming AI generation of agents," according to Intel's vice-president of AI products.

cards.headline: Fusion startup Xcimer activates world's largest privately owned laser
cards.teaser: Xcimer fired up the world's largest laser owned by a private company.
cards.body:
Xcimer, a fusion energy company, has activated what it describes as the world's largest privately owned laser. The milestone marks progress in the startup's push to develop commercial fusion energy technology using large-scale laser systems.

The achievement reflects a broader shift in fusion research, with private companies now building laser facilities that were traditionally operated by government laboratories. Xcimer joins a small group of private firms pursuing this approach to advance fusion energy development.

cards.headline: SpaceX veterans assess Blue Origin launch pad rebuild timeline
cards.teaser: Engineers with SpaceX experience are evaluating how long it will take Blue Origin to rebuild its launch pad.
cards.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded on its launch pad at Cape Canaveral, Florida on Thursday night, damaging the facility. SpaceX veterans have since offered their estimates on how long the rebuild will take.

The incident has put everyone involved in an uncomfortable position. Rebuilding a launch pad requires extensive engineering work and safety testing before the facility can be certified for flight operations again.

cards.headline: Google releases Fitbit Air blueprints for third-party accessory makers
cards.teaser: Google has published technical specifications and CAD drawings for the Fitbit Air to enable custom accessories.
cards.body:
Google released the complete technical blueprints for its Fitbit Air fitness tracker, allowing anyone to design and manufacture bands and accessories for the device. The company published CAD drawings and specifications that enable third-party manufacturers and individual makers to create compatible products.

The move opens the Fitbit Air platform to custom accessories including bicep bands and arm sleeves. Multiple publications have reported that the bicep band placement provides excellent heart rate accuracy compared to traditional wrist-worn sensors. The blueprints enable 3D printing and traditional manufacturing of accessories that fit the device.

cards.headline: Sony reveals God of War Laufey spinoff featuring Kratos' wife Faye
cards.teaser: Sony announced a new God of War game centered on Faye, the mother of Atreus and wife of Kratos.
cards.body:
Sony unveiled God of War Laufey, a spinoff game from Santa Monica Studio that will follow the character Faye, who is Kratos' late wife and the mother of Atreus. The game was announced during Sony's State of Play showcase and marks the first God of War title to center on Faye as the protagonist.

The game will be released for PlayStation 5. Footage from the announcement showed a new character named Phranque, a talking cube voiced by actor Jack Quaid. The God of War series has expanded beyond its original focus on Kratos to explore other characters from Norse mythology.

cards.headline: Insomniac reveals Marvel's Wolverine combat system and violence options
cards.teaser: Game developers at Insomniac detailed the combat mechanics and content options for their upcoming Wolverine game.
cards.body:
Insomniac Games provided an in-depth look at Marvel's Wolverine, including details on the claw combat system, X-Men cameos, and a low-gore option for players. The developers described the game as unapologetically violent in its default mode but confirmed players can reduce graphic content. The game will feature combat centered on Wolverine's claws and regenerative abilities, with mechanics that allow the character to die despite his healing factor.

The announcement came during Sony's State of Play event, which also included reveals for God of War Laufey and Until Dawn. Insomniac discussed how X-Men characters will appear in the game and detailed their approach to adapting the character for interactive gameplay on PlayStation 5.

cards.headline: Cybersecurity firm Cyera pursues funding at $12 billion valuation
cards.teaser: Cyera is closing in on a $300 million funding round that would value the company at $12 billion.
cards.body:
Cybersecurity company Cyera is nearing completion of a $300 million funding round led by Evolution Equity Partners. The investment would value the company at $12 billion, representing a valuation multiple of 80 times its annual recurring revenue.

The high valuation comes despite Cyera operating at a loss. The company specializes in data security and has attracted investor interest in a market where cybersecurity firms command premium valuations based on growth potential rather than current profitability.

hero.headline: Patriots Acquire Wide Receiver A.J. Brown from Eagles in Trade
hero.body:
The New England Patriots have acquired wide receiver A.J. Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles in a trade, the team announced. Brown, a three-time Pro Bowl selection, joins the Patriots after spending the past several seasons with the Eagles. The move addresses a key need for New England's receiving corps and reunites Brown with his childhood favorite team.

Brown expressed enthusiasm about joining the Patriots, describing himself as being in awe to play for the team he rooted for growing up. However, he declined to discuss the circumstances surrounding his departure from Philadelphia. The trade has generated mixed reactions among Eagles players during organized team activities, according to reports.

The acquisition marks a significant shift for both franchises. Brown has been one of the league's most productive receivers in recent years, providing a proven downfield threat and red zone target. His addition gives the Patriots a veteran presence in the receiving room and addresses concerns about offensive firepower heading into the upcoming season.

Brown also addressed lingering questions about his health, stating that his knees are fine and there is nothing to worry about regarding his physical condition. The receiver has dealt with knee-related issues in the past, making his health status a key factor for the Patriots as they integrate him into their offensive scheme.

The trade represents a major roster move for New England as the team continues to retool its offense. Brown's production and experience could provide an immediate impact, though the full terms of the trade, including what assets the Patriots sent to Philadelphia, were not disclosed in the initial announcement. The move comes during the offseason program as teams prepare for the upcoming season.

cards.headline: Rams Acquired Myles Garrett from Browns After Months of Negotiations
cards.teaser: The Los Angeles Rams completed a trade for Cleveland Browns defensive end Myles Garrett after general manager Les Snead pursued the deal throughout the offseason.
cards.body:
The Los Angeles Rams traded for Cleveland Browns defensive end Myles Garrett following an extended pursuit by general manager Les Snead during the offseason. Rams rookie Jared Verse was a key component of the deal that brought one of the league's top pass rushers to Los Angeles.

The trade marks a significant move for both organizations and has generated considerable attention across the NFL. The acquisition strengthens the Rams' defensive line and reshapes the competitive landscape, particularly in the NFC West where division opponents will now face Garrett twice annually.

cards.headline: Milan Momcilovic Transfers to Kentucky Basketball from Iowa State
cards.teaser: Former Iowa State star Milan Momcilovic committed to Kentucky, choosing the Wildcats over Louisville in a recruitment that attracted significant attention.
cards.body:
Milan Momcilovic, a standout player from Iowa State, has committed to Kentucky basketball. He is scheduled to arrive on campus Saturday. The transfer came after a competitive recruitment process that included Louisville as a finalist option.

Momcilovic was among the most sought-after transfers available in the portal this offseason. His addition strengthens Kentucky's roster as the program prepares for the upcoming season.

cards.headline: Qualifier Maja Chwalinska Reaches French Open Semifinals
cards.teaser: Polish qualifier Maja Chwalinska advanced to her first Grand Slam semifinal with a victory over Anna Kalinskaya at the French Open.
cards.body:
Maja Chwalinska continued her remarkable French Open run by defeating Anna Kalinskaya in the quarterfinals to reach her first Grand Slam semifinal. The Polish qualifier has become one of the tournament's standout stories, advancing much further than qualifiers typically do in major championships.

The 5ft 5in left-hander proved too clever for Kalinskaya, using intelligence and technique to compensate for her lack of height and power. Chwalinska's tactical approach—featuring drop shots and slices—consistently disrupted her opponent's rhythm throughout the match.

cards.headline: Charles Leclerc Signs New Long-Term Contract with Ferrari
cards.teaser: Ferrari driver Charles Leclerc agreed to a new long-term deal with the team ahead of this weekend's Monaco Grand Prix.
cards.body:
Charles Leclerc has signed a new multiyear contract with Ferrari, extending his relationship with the Italian team. The 28-year-old Monegasque driver will continue alongside Lewis Hamilton, who also holds a long-term deal with the Scuderia. Ferrari announced the agreement on the eve of the Monaco Grand Prix, Leclerc's home race.

Leclerc has been with Ferrari since 2019 and has competed in 155 races for the team—a tally second only to Michael Schumacher's legendary tenure between 1996 and 2006. Currently third in this season's standings, Leclerc has become a cornerstone of Ferrari's future plans.

cards.headline: Alex Scott Set to Make England Debut in World Cup Friendlies
cards.teaser: Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott is positioned to earn his first England cap during upcoming World Cup warm-up matches in the United States.
cards.body:
Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott is poised to make his England debut in the upcoming World Cup warm-up matches in the United States. The call-up marks a significant milestone in his career.

The friendlies serve as preparation for England ahead of their World Cup campaign, providing the manager with an opportunity to assess squad options and finalize selections for the tournament.

cards.headline: Kirsty Hanson to Join Tottenham from Aston Villa
cards.teaser: Aston Villa's top scorer Kirsty Hanson is set to transfer to Tottenham following an impressive Women's Super League season.
cards.body:
Aston Villa forward Kirsty Hanson is moving to Tottenham after an impressive season in the Women's Super League. Hanson was Villa's top scorer this campaign, establishing herself as a key player for the midlands club.

The transfer sees Hanson step up to join the north London side as they continue to build their squad for the upcoming season.

hero.headline: Soul Singer Peabo Bryson Dies at 75
hero.body:
Peabo Bryson, the R&B singer known for his work on Disney ballads and romantic duets, has died at age 75. Celine Dion, who performed "Beauty and the Beast" with Bryson for the 1991 animated film, said she was heartbroken by his death.

Bryson won two Grammy Awards during his career and became widely recognized as the voice behind several Disney songs. He recorded "A Whole New World" from Aladdin and "Beauty and the Beast" from the film of the same name. His tenor voice and romantic ballad style earned him recognition across R&B and pop music.

The singer's career spanned decades, with his work on Disney soundtracks introducing his music to multiple generations of listeners. Both "A Whole New World" and "Beauty and the Beast" became enduring popular songs that extended beyond their original film contexts. His Grammy wins recognized his vocal performances and contributions to music.

Bryson's death was confirmed on Wednesday. Dion publicly expressed her grief over the loss of her former duet partner. The two singers collaborated on one of Disney's most recognized songs from the renaissance era of the studio's animated films.

His work in R&B and as a duet partner made him a distinctive voice in American popular music. The combination of his romantic vocal style and his association with major film soundtracks gave him a broad audience that crossed typical genre boundaries.

cards.headline: CBS News Fires 60 Minutes Correspondent Scott Pelley
cards.teaser: CBS News terminated longtime 60 Minutes correspondent Scott Pelley following a clash with network leadership.
cards.body:
CBS News fired Scott Pelley, a veteran correspondent at 60 Minutes since 2004, following a clash with network management. The termination came after Pelley confronted CBS leadership during a staff meeting, criticizing the network's recent decision to dismiss the show's executive producer, executive editor, and two fellow correspondents, Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega.

During the meeting with newly appointed executive producer Nick Bilton and CBS News managing editor Charles Forelle, Pelley directly challenged editor-in-chief Bari Weiss over the cuts to the longtime news program. The firings represent a significant overhaul at one of television's most established news shows.

cards.headline: Martin Scorsese Endorses AI as Creatively Freeing Tool
cards.teaser: Director Martin Scorsese drew criticism after endorsing artificial intelligence as a creative tool for filmmakers.
cards.body:
Martin Scorsese has become an unlikely Hollywood advocate for artificial intelligence in filmmaking. The legendary director endorsed AI as a tool that can help filmmakers work faster during pre-production without compromising quality or creative craft.

Scorsese's specific use case is storyboarding, where he sees AI as creatively freeing rather than restrictive. However, his endorsement has drawn criticism from industry professionals who view AI as problematic for creative work.

cards.headline: Spencer Pratt in Second Place in Los Angeles Mayoral Primary
cards.teaser: Reality television personality Spencer Pratt is in second place behind Karen Bass in the Los Angeles mayoral primary.
cards.body:
Spencer Pratt has secured second place in the Los Angeles mayoral primary election behind Karen Bass. The reality television personality from The Hills made an unexpected showing in the race, with his wife Heidi Montag supporting his campaign.

Pratt's campaign centered on religious messaging, citing Jesus as his role model and claiming God called him to pursue the mayoral position. During the race, he characterized some opponents as "demonic entities." He credited his wife with guiding him toward what he described as a faith-based path.

cards.headline: YouTube Star KSI Leaves Sidemen Group
cards.teaser: Social media personality KSI announced his departure from the Sidemen, a prominent YouTube collective.
cards.body:
KSI has left the Sidemen, the YouTube group he helped build into one of the platform's most successful collectives. The social media star addressed his fellow Sidemen members following his decision to quit the group.

KSI told the remaining Sidemen members that he will always be there for them despite leaving the collective. The departure marks a significant change for the YouTube group, which has produced content together for years and built a large following across social media platforms.

cards.headline: Study Finds 70 Percent of Americans Play Video Games Weekly
cards.teaser: Two-thirds of Americans play video games for at least an hour each week, according to a new industry report.
cards.body:
A new report from the Entertainment Software Association found that approximately 70 percent of Americans play video games for at least an hour each week. The study, published Wednesday, surveyed a broad demographic across the country.

The findings underscore how deeply video games have become integrated into American entertainment habits, reaching people across different age groups and lifestyles.

cards.headline: Giorgio Locatelli Replaces John Torode on Celebrity MasterChef
cards.teaser: Italian restaurateur Giorgio Locatelli will co-host Celebrity MasterChef alongside Grace Dent.
cards.body:
Giorgio Locatelli will join Grace Dent as co-host of Celebrity MasterChef. The Italian restaurateur replaces John Torode, who exited the series last year.

Locatelli brings restaurant industry experience to the cooking competition show. Dent and Locatelli will lead the celebrity edition of the popular British cooking program going forward. Torode had been a longtime host of the MasterChef franchise before his departure.

hero.headline: Justice Department cancels Trump administration anti-weaponization fund
hero.teaser: The Justice Department scrapped plans for a fund the Trump administration had proposed to address what it called weaponization of government.
hero.body:
The Justice Department has scrapped a 1.8 billion dollar fund that the Trump administration had created to address what it called the weaponization of government agencies. Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche announced the decision to abandon the program, which faced mounting criticism from lawmakers and legal challenges.

The fund represented a key Trump administration initiative aimed at investigating and potentially compensating individuals who alleged they had been targeted by federal investigative and prosecutorial powers. The cancellation marks a significant reversal of one of the administration's stated priorities regarding federal law enforcement agencies.

Blanche's announcement to drop the fund came after considerable pushback from top Republican lawmakers, suggesting internal disagreement within the administration about the program's direction and viability. The initiative had also faced scrutiny in Congress and legal challenges in the courts, which complicated efforts to implement it.

The anti-weaponization fund emerged from Trump administration concerns about federal agencies, particularly the Justice Department and FBI, and their use of investigative powers. Officials argued the program would provide recourse for individuals who believed they had been unfairly targeted through criminal investigations or prosecutions.

The decision to eliminate the fund reflects a broader reassessment of policies from the Trump administration's previous term. As new officials took control of the Justice Department, they evaluated various initiatives inherited from the earlier administration and made determinations about which programs to continue or discontinue.

The timing of the announcement suggests that practical and political obstacles made sustaining the fund difficult. Congressional opposition from within Republican ranks indicated that not all party members supported the initiative, while court challenges questioned its legal foundation.

The Justice Department and other administration officials did not immediately provide detailed public statements explaining the specific reasoning behind the cancellation decision beyond acknowledging that the fund would no longer proceed. The move left questions about what would happen to any preliminary work or resources already allocated to the program.

This decision follows a period in which the Justice Department under Trump administration leadership had launched numerous criminal investigations into political opponents and critics, including former FBI director James Comey, New York Attorney General Letitia James, and various Democratic members of Congress. These investigations have not yet resulted in convictions.

The cancellation of the anti-weaponization fund represents one of several policy reversals and adjustments as the Trump administration entered its second term. Officials continued evaluating which previous administration policies would remain in place and which would be abandoned or significantly reformed.

cards.headline: Primary elections conclude in six states with key Democratic and Republican nominations decided
cards.teaser: Polls closed Tuesday in six states holding primary elections, with voters selecting nominees for Senate, gubernatorial, and congressional races ahead of the 202.
cards.body:
Polls closed Tuesday in six states holding primary elections to select nominees for Senate, gubernatorial, and congressional races ahead of the 2026 general election. In Iowa, Josh Turek secured the Democratic Senate nomination, defeating a rival who had criticized party leaders. Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor, positioning herself as the likely favorite in the general election.

In California, vote counting continued in major statewide races. Xavier Becerra and Steve Hilton led their respective Democratic and Republican primaries for governor, vying to replace term-limited Governor Gavin Newsom. Final results remained uncalled as of reporting time.

cards.headline: White House moves to centralize control over federal science grants
cards.teaser: The Office of Management and Budget is seeking greater authority over billions of dollars in federal research funding, drawing criticism from scientists.
cards.body:
The White House Office of Management and Budget has proposed sweeping changes to federal grant administration that would require all grants approved by Trump's political appointees to "demonstrably advance the president's policy priorities." Under the new rules, officials would vet grants from universities and nongovernmental organizations based on their alignment with "American values" as defined by the president.

The proposal has triggered widespread concern among scientists and experts who warn it would fundamentally undermine how federal research funding has been distributed for decades. Critics argue the changes would compromise scientific integrity by introducing political considerations into decisions traditionally made through peer review and merit-based evaluation.

cards.headline: Trump administration shapes America's 250th anniversary celebration with new events and branding
cards.teaser: The White House has created highly visible, centrally controlled events for the nation's semiquincentennial, many established by presidential directive.
cards.body:
The White House has organized a series of highly visible, centrally controlled events for America's 250th birthday celebration in 2026. Many of these events were created through presidential directive and emphasize spectacle, branding, and new traditions for the milestone anniversary.

The administration's hands-on approach to planning the semiquincentennial observances represents a departure from how previous major national anniversaries have been commemorated.

cards.headline: Centrist Democrats launch pledge supporting capitalism over socialism
cards.teaser: Two Democratic House members who won Republican-held seats are circulating a vow committing signatories to moderate economic policies.
cards.body:
A pair of Democratic House members who flipped Republican-held seats are launching a new pledge for party colleagues to sign, explicitly stating their support for capitalist rather than socialist economic policies. The initiative seeks to position participating Democrats as moderates on economic issues.

The pledge represents an effort by centrist members to distinguish themselves from progressive Democrats who have advocated for expanded government programs and stronger regulation of businesses. The two representatives are asking other Democrats to join them in signing the statement as they seek to appeal to swing voters ahead of the midterm elections.

cards.headline: Florida Republicans pursue artificial intelligence regulations as DeSantis prepares to leave office
cards.teaser: Top Florida Republican leaders are pushing to expand rules on AI, including chatbots, despite pushback from the Trump administration.
cards.body:
Leading Florida Republicans are intensifying their push to regulate artificial intelligence as Governor Ron DeSantis, a vocal critic of the technology, nears the end of his term. State party leaders and candidates are promising to increase restrictions on AI applications, including chatbot technology.

The Florida Republican effort to expand AI regulation comes as the Trump administration has resisted similar federal restrictions on the technology. The divergence highlights a split within the party over how to approach AI governance, with Florida Republicans pursuing state-level controls despite opposition from the White House.

cards.headline: California governor primary results remain uncalled as Hilton and Becerra lead early returns
cards.teaser: Vote counting continues in California's gubernatorial primary, where Democrats and Republicans are selecting nominees to replace term-limited Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Steve Hilton held an early lead among Republican candidates, while Xavier Becerra led among Democrats in California's gubernatorial primary. The race will determine which two candidates advance to November's general election, regardless of party affiliation, under California's top-two primary system.

Democrats Katie Porter and Tom Steyer competed alongside Becerra for their party's nomination, while Republican Chad Bianco challenged Hilton. The primary election will set up the general election to replace Governor Gavin Newsom, who is term-limited.
